featured_reviews.name: Omkar Naik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dan Dan Chinese today on the occasion of Ram Navami, as many nearby Chinese food corners were closed. I decided to give this place a try, and I ordered two dishes: American Choupsey and Chicken Hakka Noodles.

Both dishes were delicious, and I must say, it was my first time trying Choupsey, which I highly recommend to anyone visiting this place. The Chicken Hakka Noodles were also tasty, and they offer good quality and quantity. The portion sizes are quite generous, so one person may struggle to finish a dish — it's best to come with a companion or plan to parcel the leftover food.

As a local guide on Google Maps and someone who likes to share detailed reviews, I'd like to highlight a few points that may be helpful for potential customers, and also for the owner to consider:

1. Lack of Air Conditioning: There is no air conditioning in the restaurant, and in the humid climate of Vile Parle East, it can get uncomfortable, especially near the fan area. Adding an air conditioning system could significantly improve the dining experience.

2. Cold Drinks: The restaurant doesn't offer cold drinks on the menu but provides them by bringing them from an outside source. While I appreciate that they offer this option when many others refuse, it would be more convenient if they stocked cold drinks on-site.

3. Slow Service: The food took quite a long time to be served, and there was no dedicated staff member to assist customers. There was an uncle helping out, but he was juggling multiple tasks — taking orders, answering calls, handling the kitchen, and managing bills. This made the service a bit frustrating at times, and I ended up packing my noodles to go. It would be beneficial to have an extra staff member to assist with customer service.

4. Mosquitoes: The restaurant is open, and with no gates, mosquitoes can be a problem. The plants outside, while adding to the aesthetic, also provide a hiding place for mosquitoes. Addressing this issue, perhaps with a net or better control, would improve the comfort of diners.

5. Order Assistance: Typically, restaurants guide customers on specials, combos, and menu items when taking orders. However, I was not informed about the combos or daily specials until after my order was placed. It would be helpful if the staff proactively shared this information to enhance the dining experience.

6. Customer Service: While the food was good, there were some basic service issues. No one asked if I wanted water, and there were no tissues or sauces available on the table. That said, I’d like to commend the uncle at the counter, who made an effort to clean my plate, spoon, and fork before serving. His politeness and attention to detail were appreciated.

Suggestions for Improvement:

Install air conditioning to improve comfort in the humid climate.

Stock cold drinks on-site to make it more convenient for customers.

Reduce the waiting time and consider adding more staff for customer service.

Address the mosquito issue, perhaps with better pest control or netting.

Ensure that customers are informed about specials and combos when ordering.

Provide basic amenities like water, tissues, and sauces to enhance the overall dining experience.

Overall, Dan Dan Chinese offers tasty food, but there are some areas for improvement, especially regarding service, comfort, and customer care. With a few adjustments, it could provide a much more enjoyable dining experience.

Note: I’ve added photos of the restaurant, the food I ordered, and the menu for reference to help others get a better idea before visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Anand Tiwari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fumi at Sahara Star is an absolute gem for anyone who loves Pan-Asian cuisine. Located inside the luxurious 5-star Sahara Star hotel in Mumbai, this restaurant offers not just food, but an experience.

I began my evening with their Berry Blast mocktail, a refreshing burst of fruity sweetness and tang. Made with fresh strawberries and lime juice, it was beautifully presented and instantly set the tone for the meal.

Next came the Hot & Sour Soup, perfectly balanced with spice, tang, and warmth — just the kind of comfort you’d expect from an authentic Asian kitchen.

Then arrived the Dimsum Sampler, and I must say it was a treat both to the eyes and the palate. From prawn and chicken to vegetarian delights like avocado cream cheese and truffle-infused dumplings — each one was delicate, flavorful, and perfectly steamed.

The star of the evening was definitely the Sushi Boat. Served in a wooden boat, it featured an assortment of beautifully crafted sushi rolls — from creamy avocado and cheese maki to crispy tempura rolls and prawn-filled delights. Every bite was fresh, balanced, and bursting with umami.

For the main course, I went with the Wok Mixed Vegetables in Spicy Black Bean Sauce paired with Burnt Garlic Fried Rice. The vegetables were crisp and coated in a deliciously smoky sauce, while the rice had just the right amount of garlic and crunch. The presentation was top-notch, and what made it even better was the live open kitchen, where you can see the chefs at work — it’s such a joy to watch your food being prepared right in front of you.

To end this wonderful meal, I indulged in the Miso Crème Brûlée — silky, caramelized perfection with a subtle Asian twist. It was the perfect finale to an exceptional dining experience.

From start to finish, Fumi impressed me with its attention to detail, authentic flavours, and stunning presentation. Whether you’re a sushi lover, dimsum enthusiast, or simply looking for an elegant Asian dining experience in Mumbai — Fumi at Sahara Star is an absolute must-visit. 🍣✨

NEW PLACE ALERT*

Located in Vile Parle East, this restaurant and bar serves some amazingly fresh and quality dishes. The primary cuisine served is North Indian and Chinese. They also have Mangalorean dishes on the menu which are a must try. They have a nice bar with a wide variety of drinks to choose from.
The ambience is nice with dim lights and a wall full of quotes. The seating is comfortable. The overall look and feel is like a family restaurant and bar. The service was prompt to start with Mahesh taking down the orders. However they took a reasonable amount of time to get all the dishes.

The mocktails we had were Cinderella and Berry Blast. Both these were juice based drinks. Berry blast has Cranberry and Apple juice with a touch of honey.
Cindrella has orange juice and fresh lime which makes it very refreshing.

The food we had was all very good in terms of quality and quantity. I would rate it a value for money place.

We had Murg Toorki which was Chicken Tikka marinated with Cheese and this was delicious. The chicken was cooked to perfection, juicy and charred perfectly. This tasted even better with the mint coriander chutney.

Coriander Chicken Dry was a Chinese appetizer, this was again very good. Herbaceous flavour with garlic and spring onions. Again well cooked Chicken. Very satisfying.

For the main course we had Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa. My favourite and everything was perfect. Must have when here. Highly recommended.

The Cheese Garlic Naan here is not the usual Naan with the Garlic and Cheese outside. Here it's stuffed inside and is very wholesome.
We had Chicken Betabi which is a red gravy similar to Butter Chicken in many ways with shredded chicken in a luscious velvety gravy.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

This place even has outdoor seating which is accessible only post rains. I am totally in awe of the simplicity and the no nonsense kind of approach to serving good quality food.

I am totally coming back here again with my gang for a great meal.

Till next time Bon Appetit!

Celebrating the spirit of Onam in the grandeur of Sahara Star was truly a delightful experience. The plush property, located right next to Mumbai’s domestic airport, set the perfect stage for a festive indulgence. The lavish Sunday Brunch at The Earth Plate – Global Cuisine transformed into a traditional Kerala Sadhya spread, offering an authentic taste of heritage served with warmth and elegance.

The banana leaf thali came alive with a vibrant array of curries, pachadis, thorans, avial, olan, sambar, rasam, pulisery, and fluffy red rice – each dish bursting with homely flavors, perfectly balanced spices, and that comforting touch of Kerala’s culinary roots. Crisp papadams, tangy pickles, and steaming hot appams completed the meal, while payasam and other Indian sweets brought the feast to a heavenly close.

The buffet around the restaurant was equally indulgent, showcasing a harmony of regional Indian delicacies, global favorites, and stunning desserts – all beautifully curated in a festive floral setting that reflected the joy of Onam. The live counters, attentive chefs, and vibrant ambiance added to the overall charm, making it an immersive dining experience.

✨ From the soulful flavors on the leaf to the elegant hospitality and plush surroundings, the Onam Sadhya at Sahara Star was more than just a meal – it was a cultural celebration plated with luxury. A must-experience brunch that beautifully bridges tradition with fine dining in the heart of Mumbai.

Overall, a wonderful place for a family celebration, and I’ll definitely recommend Earth Plate to others.

Asia Kitchen by Mainland China, Goregaon East — we went after ages. And before you ask, yes, hope was cautiously packed along with appetite.

First pleasant surprise? A proper menu card. A real, hold-it-in-your-hand, flip-the-pages menu. Not a QR code that demands network, patience and reading glasses. In 2026, this felt revolutionary.

We began with the Vietnamese chicken noodle soup — light, comforting, refreshingly gentle. The kind that doesn’t shout, just quietly does its job. Very demure. Very mindful.

Next came the mushroom cheung fun — soft, silky Hong Kong–style rice rolls that almost redeemed the evening. Moist, delicate, flavourful. The kind of dish that makes you pause mid-sentence.

Then the mains arrived. Five-spice grilled lamb chops. Flavour? Lovely. Texture? The lamb appears to have gone to the gym before arriving on my plate. Chewy is polite. It was less “cut with a knife” and more “earn your protein.” Two pieces at ₹600-plus-tax — that’s ₹300 per chop. At that price, I expect tenderness. Not a jawline workout. The poor lamb gave its life. It needn’t have done so in vain!

The asparagus and sun-dried tomato jasmine fried rice was… philosophical. Four heads of asparagus, five minuscule bits of sun-dried tomato and some green apple — though there were more letters in “green apple” than actual pieces of green apple. It was like playing culinary treasure hunt!

Service was okayish, despite only four tables being occupied. They added a discretionary service charge, which they waived off without drama when asked — so points for that.

Overall? Portions have shrunk. Prices have grown. Enthusiasm has… adjusted accordingly.

We went to Asia Kitchen after a long time. We’ll be going again after a long time more.

This restaurant is a fantastic choice for Chinese cuisine, standing out for both its flavors and service. With a price of ₹2000+ for two, it offers good value for the quality provided. One visit is sure to make you come back for more!

Food:
Having explored various Chinese dishes before, we decided to rely on the server’s recommendations, and they did not disappoint! The food was served piping hot, bursting with flavors. Do note that some items may be discontinued or unavailable at times, depending on the menu updates.

Soups: The Veg Eight Treasure Soup was a great way to kickstart the meal, setting the perfect tone.

Starters: The Crispy Corn Chilly Pepper had a unique crunch and was full of flavor.

Main Course: The Veg Lemon Grass Fried Rice carried a subtle yet delightful lemongrass aroma. The Veg Nasi Goreng had a well-balanced taste, and the Stir-Fried Chicken with Chilly Garlic & Hot Basil was delicious, though the texture was slightly inconsistent.

Curries & Noodles: The Chicken Thai Red Curry had a rich taste, but the boiled chicken didn’t do it justice—battered pieces would be a better alternative. The Lotus Stem & Asparagus in Red Curry Infusion is a must-try if you enjoy bold flavors. The Wok Tossed Noodles were fairly standard Hakka noodles. The Stir-Fried Crabmeat in Thai Yellow Curry was quite spicy but became well-balanced when mixed with a coconut base. The Crispy Chicken Katsu Baos were decent but could be elevated with the addition of flavorful sauces.

Desserts: The Caramel Sponge Cake with Toffee Sauce was soft and delicious, while the Chocolate Rolls with Ice Cream had a rich Nutella filling. The newly introduced Mango Pudding is definitely worth trying. The Chocolate Dome, while an impressive concept, felt a bit too much to finish after a full meal.

❌ Let-down: Eggwhite Fried Rice and the Chinese New Year Special Potato Dish.

Service:
